items.question: What is a cache eviction policy?
items.answer: When the cache is full it removes an entry to make room for a new one.
items.reference: An eviction policy decides which entry to remove when the cache is full. Least recently used removes the entry that has gone longest without being read. A time to live expires an entry after a fixed period whether or not it is full. The cache hit ratio is the share of reads served from the cache.

items.question: What does a p-value tell you?
items.answer: How likely data this extreme would be if the null hypothesis were true.
items.reference: The significance level is the threshold, often 0.05, below which a p-value leads you to reject the null hypothesis. Running many tests at once inflates the chance of a false alarm; this is the multiple comparisons problem.

memory.quote: A confidence interval gives a range of plausible values for the true effect.
memory.subject: confidence intervals

bad.q: How does your confidence interval analysis use the significance level?
bad.why: an explanation of a concept presented as their own analysis

bad.q: How does a significance level of 0.05 hold when the null hypothesis is both true and false?

items.question: What is a layer in a container image?
items.answer: Each instruction in the Dockerfile adds a layer on top of the previous one.
items.reference: Docker reuses an unchanged layer from the build cache, so instructions that change rarely should come first. A multi-stage build compiles in one stage and copies only the result into a small final image.

items.question: What is a race condition?
items.answer: Two threads change shared data at the same time and the result depends on timing.
items.reference: A mutex lets only one thread at a time enter the critical section that touches the shared data. An atomic operation completes as one indivisible step, so no other thread sees it half done.
